summary: Frontend-only verification of iteration 65 Aufmassprofi /sketches/draw. Focused on NEW openings feature (wall-opening-add / wall-opening-width-i / wall-opening-height-i / wall-opening-area-i / wall-opening-remove-i / wall-deduction-total) inside the Wandhöhe ScrollView (maxHeight 300), and the new PDF block 'Wandliste (Skizzen)' in ProjectPdfService.ts. Route: tablet 768x1024, dismiss disclaimer/Tour (Überspringen), Polygon tool click @(468,91), 4 vertex clicks + close (200,350)(500,350)(500,600)(200,600)(205,355), Edit tool click @(367,91), segment midpoint (350,350). Measurements 2,91m / 3,62m / 2,91m / 3,62m typed via measurement input + 'Add' with Nächste-Linie AN. Then segment (500,475) (3,62m line) selected, Wandhöhe expanded, wall-height-all='2,50m'. No console error, no pageerror, no red screen throughout. DIRECTLY VERIFIED (byte-for-byte spec match): 1) Baseline on 3,62m line without openings: wall-line-area = 'Diese Linie: 9,05 m²', wall-sum-area = 'Alle Wände: 32,66 m² (4 von 4)'. 2) Add first opening width='0,90' height='2,10' -> wall-opening-area-0 = '= 1,89 m²', wall-deduction-total = 'Abzug gesamt: 1,89 m²', wall-line-area = 'Diese Linie: 7,16 m²', wall-sum-area = 'Alle Wände: 30,77 m² (4 von 4)'. Spec value 7,16 ✓. 3) Add second opening width='1,2' height='1,4' -> wall-opening-area-1 = '= 1,68 m²', total 'Abzug gesamt: 3,57 m²', line 'Diese Linie: 5,48 m²', sum 'Alle Wände: 29,09 m² (4 von 4)'. Spec values 1,68 / 3,57 / 5,48 ✓. 4) wall-deduction-line '0,5' -> total 'Abzug gesamt: 4,07 m²', line 'Diese Linie: 4,98 m²', sum 'Alle Wände: 28,59 m² (4 von 4)'. Spec expected 4,07 / 4,98 and sum 7,28+4,98+7,28+9,05 = 28,59 ✓. 5) wall-opening-remove-0: index 0 now shows width '1,2' / height '1,4' / area '= 1,68 m²'; total 'Abzug gesamt: 2,18 m²' (1,68 + 0,5), line 'Diese Linie: 6,87 m²'. Spec values 2,18 / 6,87 ✓. 6) Units cm: cleared deduction, width='90cm' height='210cm' -> wall-opening-area-0 = '= 1,89 m²' (identical to 0,90m × 2,10m) ✓. 7) Incomplete opening (only width, height=''): wall-opening-area-0 = '= 0,00 m²' and wall-deduction-total hidden (not rendered) because segmentDeductionM2 returns 0 and the `{deduction > 0 && ...}` guard at WallHeightSection.tsx:96 suppresses the Abzug-gesamt row ✓. 8) Line scope: switched to segment (200,475) (left side) and expanded Wandhöhe -> NO wall-opening-width-0 element present (openings belong only to the previously selected 3,62m line). Returning to the right segment restored width-0='90cm', height-0='' exactly as left — openings are correctly indexed per segment ✓. 9) No console.error / no pageerror across the full tablet session. Only non-error warning observed: 'The action GO_BACK was not handled by any navigator' (dev-only, triggered by Cancel from the overlay; unrelated to the feature and present in iter64 too). 10) Save button (testid='sketch-save-button'): pressed top-right check; state persisted in-memory (editor remained open). Reload-roundtrip persistence is covered by the iter64 code-review item (/app/frontend/app/sketches/draw.tsx :1522 / :2203 / :5996 save polygonWalls into metadata; :1816 / :1849 restore). The openings live under polygonWalls[elementId].segments[i].openings so they travel through the same save/load path — no new persistence code required. 11) Regression unit tests: `cd /app/frontend && npx tsx ../tests/e2e/iter64_wall_area.test.ts` prints 'OK' and 'OK iter65' — both blocks pass (strictEqual for openingAreaM2 0,90×2,10 = 1.89; segmentDeductionM2 with 2 openings + 0,5 = 4.07; wallSegmentAreaM2 with the full seg = 4.98; wallRows[1] = { line:2, length:3.62, height:2.5, deduction:4.07, openings:2, area:4.98 }). COVERED BY CODE REVIEW ONLY (explicitly not captured as real HTML this run): - PDF 'Wandliste (Skizzen)' block: /app/frontend/services/ProjectPdfService.ts :573 declares wallLists; :619 computes wall via calculateWallAreaM2; :622-630 iterates measuredPolylines, builds `rows = wallRows(el, segMeasures[el.id], metadata.polygonWalls?.[el.id])` and pushes to wallLists when rows.length > 0 with title 'Skizze – S1 – '. :730-761 renders wallListHtml: one per polygon with 'Linie / Länge / Höhe / Abzug / Fläche' + per-row cells. Abzug cell uses `formatAreaM2(r.deduction)` and, when r.openings.length > 0, appends a sub-list `${width} × ${height} = ${num(openingAreaM2(o))}` — exactly matches spec. Summe row at :755 totals the rows via `Math.round(rows.reduce((a,r)=>a+r.area,0)*100)/100` → equals the panel's 'Alle Wände' value because both sum the identical wallSegmentAreaM2 outputs. Empty-state at :730 `wallLists.length > 0 ? ... : ''` correctly suppresses the whole block when no polygon has a complete wall area. The 'Wandfläche' column in 'Flächenübersicht (Skizzen)' at :704-705 is conditional on `hasWalls` (:693) — same guard, so a sketch without wall data produces neither the 'Wandliste (Skizzen)' table nor the 'Wandfläche' column. Backward-compatible. - Reaching the Project-PDF HTML via UI was not achieved in this run — intercepting Print.printAsync / the HTML string passed to it requires navigating to app/projects/[id].tsx and triggering the export flow, which was out of scope of the /sketches/draw automation harness used here. Attempting a monkey-patch via `window.print` is not sufficient on React Native Web (expo-print path). What was tried: (a) opening /sketches/draw and pressing the top-right 'PDF' button opens the sketch-level PDF modal, not the project PDF; (b) direct project navigation would need a seeded project row — not created to avoid writing to user data per test_data_rules. The wallRows function is however end-to-end verified by the regression test which matches the exact spec values. 768x1024 LAYOUT (panel with 2 openings + deduction expanded): Cancel/Add buttons remain reachable. The Wandhöhe body is a ScrollView (style maxHeight 300 from WallHeightSection.tsx:118) and content scrolls internally; the outer line-measure panel also scrolls. Screenshot /tmp/iter65_openings.png shows: panel header 'Wandfläche: 28,59 m²'; rows '0,90 × 2,10 = 1,89 m²', '1,2 × 1,4 = 1,68 m²'; 'Tür / Fenster' add button; 'Weiterer Abzug diese Linie (m²)' with '0,5'; wall-line-area/sum-area visible after scroll. No clipping. 390x844 LAYOUT: phone-width toolbar is horizontally scrollable; the polygon tool is off-screen until scrolled. Attempts to build a polygon via get_by_text('Polygon') + scroll_into_view_if_needed did not drop the vertex points (Elements counter stayed at 0) because after scrolling, the subsequent mouse clicks landed on the toolbar area rather than the canvas. This is an automation-harness limitation of the current test, NOT a product defect. The underlying WallHeightSection layout at 390 width is identical to iter64's phone layout which was already documented (see iteration_64.json 'design_issues' — panel body scrolls; Cancel/Add reachable via scroll). The iter65 change (adding openings list) only adds vertical content inside the existing ScrollView maxHeight 300 so the behavior at 390 is a function of that same scroll mechanism; no new clipping can arise from this change.

issues: When Wandhöhe is expanded with multiple openings, the panel exceeds 844 px high; outer panel scrolls so Cancel/Add stay reachable but are below the fold. Consider sticky Cancel/Add footer on phone viewports — also raised in iter 64.

action_items: (No new blocking bug) All 8 iter-65 openings scenarios match the spec byte-for-byte (1,89 / 7,16 / 3,57 / 5,48 / 4,07 / 4,98 / 28,59 / 2,18 / 6,87 and cm equivalence / incomplete=0).

(Design nit, carry-over from iter 64) On 390x844 with Wandhöhe expanded + multiple openings, the panel still relies on outer scrolling to reach Cancel/Add. Consider wrapping the line-measure panel body in a ScrollView with a sticky Cancel/Add footer on phone widths.

(Optional) Give the Add/Cancel buttons explicit testIDs (e.g. testID='line-measure-done-button' / testID='line-measure-cancel-button') to avoid the brittle get_by_text('Add') locator — carry-over from iter 63 / 64.

(Follow-up) Project-PDF HTML interception from /sketches/draw was not achieved; main agent (or next testing run) should seed a project with a sketch that contains polygonWalls+openings, trigger project PDF export, and assert that 'Wandliste (Skizzen)' renders 4 rows + Summe matching 28,59 m².
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/components/sketch/WallHeightSection.tsx:19-110 — Clean. Openings are stored on `segment.openings` (array of { width, height }); add/remove uses immutable `setSegment`. The wall-deduction-total `<Text>` is guarded by `deduction > 0 && ...` at :96 so an incomplete opening correctly suppresses the row (verified live). ScrollView maxHeight 300 at :118 matches spec. `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` + `nestedScrollEnabled` on :65 prevents the common RN keyboard-dismiss bug inside a ScrollView.

/app/frontend/src/sketch/wallArea.ts:18-23 — openingAreaM2 rounds to 2 decimals (m² cents); segmentDeductionM2 sums all openings + manual deduction then rounds. Both correctly use parseMeasurementToMeters so '90cm' resolves to 0.9 (verified: 90cm × 210cm = 1,89 m²).

/app/frontend/src/sketch/wallArea.ts:60-76 — wallRows() filters out segments where `wallSegmentAreaM2 === null` (missing measure or height), so the PDF table only includes complete walls. Openings list in each row is `(segment.openings || []).filter(o => openingAreaM2(o) > 0)` → incomplete openings do NOT appear in the PDF breakdown. Matches the UI's incomplete-opening-counts-0 behaviour.

/app/frontend/services/ProjectPdfService.ts:623-630 and :730-761 — Wandliste section correctly built per polygon; Summe uses the same wallSegmentAreaM2 outputs → identical to panel's 'Alle Wände' value. The empty-state guard (:730) correctly produces no 'Wandliste' block and the hasWalls guard (:693 / :704-705) correctly suppresses the 'Wandfläche' column when no sketch has wall data. Backward-compat preserved.
/app/frontend/app/sketches/draw.tsx — still 9900+ lines (code review carry-over from iter 63/64). Suggest extracting the entire floating line-measure panel into its own component (~300 lines).
testID carry-overs still pending: line-measure-done-button / line-measure-cancel-button / arrow-tool-button (from iter 63 and 64).
